mainTopic: When a borrower must pay for a broken or dead borrowed item, the exemptions of מתה מחמת מלאכה and שאילה בבעלים, and a new משנה on a cow that was both borrowed and rented
overview: This amud finishes the story of the borrowed ax: the הלכה follows רב כהנא and רב אסי, so the borrower returns the broken pieces and pays the missing value. Then come stories about the rule of מתה מחמת מלאכה. A borrowed pail that broke is exempt if witnesses show it was used normally. A borrowed cat that died from the mice, told in two versions, is answered with the saying 'no judgment and no judge.' Next, רבא teaches how the rule of שאילה בבעלים works in practice. Asking the lender to pour water at the moment of borrowing exempts the borrower, unless the lender says 'borrow first.' Town workers count as working for the townspeople during their work hours. רבא refuses to call himself 'lent' to his students, and the גמרא limits his answer to the days outside the כלה. The story of מרימר's mule shows that the owner only checking the load does not count as בבעלים, and the story is retold as a theft case to explain why רבא was embarrassed. Finally, a new משנה opens about a cow that was both borrowed and rented and then died, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב's students question his ax ruling, and רב is silent
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי finish their challenge to רב's ruling on the broken ax by asking 'Is this the law?' רב does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: [They asked רב:] Is this the law? And רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge that started just before this section. רב's students ask whether his ruling on the broken ax is really the law, and רב gives no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רב had ruled on a borrowed ax that broke. His students question whether the borrower must really pay the way רב said. רב's silence is a signal that he accepts their point, and this sets up the ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this the law? (a challenge to a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the end of a challenge that began before this section, about the borrowed ax.

phrases.english: Is the law like this?
And Rav was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the students' challenge to רב's earlier ruling on the borrowed ax.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling on how the borrower must pay for the broken ax.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The students doubt that the law really demands payment the way רב ruled, since the broken ax still has some value.

steps.title: The law: return the broken tool and pay the missing value
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב כהנא and רב אסי. The borrower gives back the broken pieces and pays the difference up to the tool's full value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The law follows רב כהנא and רב אסי: he gives back the broken pieces and makes up the rest of the tool's value in money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that the law follows the students, not רב's first ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broken pieces are still worth something, so the owner takes them back. The borrower only pays what is missing to reach the value the tool had before it broke. He does not have to supply a whole, sound tool, as רב had ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: and he fills in (makes up the difference)

steps.whatToRemember: When a borrowed tool breaks and the borrower is responsible, he returns the broken pieces plus money to make up the tool's full value.

phrases.english: And the law is like Rav Kahana and Rav Asi,
that he returns to him its broken pieces
and makes up for him the value of the tool.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the challenge in favor of the students.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The borrower returns the broken item and pays the difference to its full prior value.

steps.title: A borrowed pail that broke: bring witnesses and be exempt
steps.stepSummary: A borrowed pail broke. רב פפא told the borrower that if he brings witnesses showing he used it normally, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man borrowed a pail from his friend and it broke. He came before רב פפא, who told him: bring witnesses that you did not use it in an unusual way, and you will be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story with a practical ruling from רב פפא about a pail that broke while it was borrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower is usually responsible even for accidents. The exception is מתה מחמת מלאכה: if the item breaks just from the normal use it was borrowed for, the borrower is exempt. Witnesses who show he used it normally put this case into that exception.

keyTerms.meaning: you changed (used it in an unusual way)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exemption of מתה מחמת מלאכה applies to borrowed tools, not only to animals, as long as there is proof of normal use.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּשְׁאֵיל דַּוְולָא מֵחַבְרֵיהּ, אִיתְּבַר.
phrases.english: A certain man borrowed a pail from his friend; it broke.
He came before Rav Pappa.
He said to him: Bring witnesses
that you did not change in its use, and be exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּשְׁאֵיל דַּוְולָא מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ax case to a new practical case about a borrowed item that broke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower whose borrowed item broke is exempt if witnesses show he used it normally.

steps.title: A borrowed cat killed by mice: does it count as dying from its work?
steps.stepSummary: A borrowed cat was killed by mice that ganged up on it. רב אשי asks whether this counts as dying from its normal work.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man borrowed a cat from his friend. The mice ganged up on it and killed it. רב אשי sat and asked: in a case like this, what is the law? Is it like an animal that died from its work, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story, and רב אשי raises a real question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cat was borrowed to catch mice, and it died while doing that job. But being killed by the very mice it was supposed to hunt is strange. So it is unclear whether this falls under the exemption of מתה מחמת מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised a question (a real doubt)
died because of its normal work (the borrower is exempt)

phrases.english: A certain man borrowed a cat from his friend,
mice banded together against it and killed it.
Rav Ashi sat and raised a question:
In a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מֵתָה מֵחֲמַת מְלָאכָה דָּמֵי, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Is it like one that died because of its work, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב אָשֵׁי וְקָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like the pail story, this tests the edges of the exemption for damage caused by normal use.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a borrowed cat killed by the mice it was hunting counts as מתה מחמת מלאכה.

steps.title: A man killed by women: the case is obvious
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי answers רב אשי with a saying in the name of רבא: a man killed by women needs no court and no judge. The point is that the cat case is obvious and needs no real ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: אבימי from הגרוניא said this in the name of רבא: a man whom women killed needs no judgment and no judge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי answers רב אשי's question with a short, sharp saying that means 'this case is obvious.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as there is nothing to debate about a man killed by women, there is nothing to debate about a cat killed by mice. On the reading followed here, a cat dying while hunting mice is simply part of the job it was borrowed for. So it counts as מתה מחמת מלאכה, and the borrower is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: no judgment and no judge (an obvious case)

steps.whatToRemember: A borrower is exempt when the borrowed item breaks or dies from the normal use it was borrowed for. Witnesses can prove this, as with the pail, and a cat killed by mice is treated as an obvious case.
steps.confusionAlert: The saying about women is not a ruling about women at all. It is a figure of speech that means 'this case is too obvious to need a court.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבִימִי מֵהַגְרוֹנְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: So said Avimi of Hagronya in the name of Rava:
A man whom women killed —
there is no judgment and no judge.
phrases.notes: He means there is nothing to decide here. The cat case is just as obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question about the cat.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is obvious and needs no court. A cat killed by the mice it was hunting is treated as dying from its work, so the borrower is exempt.

steps.title: A second version: the cat ate too many mice
steps.stepSummary: According to another version, the cat was not attacked. It ate too many mice, got sick, and died. רב אשי asks what the law is in such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the story went like this: the cat ate a lot of mice, got sick, and died. רב אשי sat and thought about it: in a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells the cat story in a different way and asks the question again. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, mice ganged up on the cat. Here the cat itself overate, so its death came from its own behavior. רב אשי wants to know if the borrower must pay for a death like this.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
It ate many mice
phrases.notes: 'It' is the borrowed cat from the story before.

phrases.english: and was harmed and died.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב אָשֵׁי וְקָא מְעַיֵּין בַּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi sat and deliberated about it:
In a case like this, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲכַל עַכְבְּרֵי טוּבָא וַחֲבִיל וּמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the cat case from step 4 and asks the question again.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a borrower liable when the borrowed cat dies from eating too many mice?

steps.title: No judgment and no judge
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי answers with a saying of אבימי מהגרוניא: a man who was 'killed by women' has no case and no judge. The cat brought its death on itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: אבימי from הגרוניא said this: a man whom women killed has no judgment and no judge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי answers רב אשי's question with a saying. The point is that the cat caused its own death, so there is no one to put on trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who wore himself out with women has only himself to blame. The cat that overate is the same, so the borrower is not held responsible for its death. In this version אבימי מהגרוניא says the saying himself, without quoting רבא as he did in the first version.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:
Avimi of Hagronya said this:
A man whom women killed –
phrases.notes: He means a man who wore himself out with too much time with women. It was his own doing.

phrases.english: there is neither judgment nor judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבִימִי מֵהַגְרוֹנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cat caused its own death, so there is no case against the borrower.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions of the cat story, the answer is the same saying: 'no judgment and no judge.' The cat's death is not something the borrower has to answer for.

steps.title: The borrower's trick: 'Pour me water'
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a borrower who wants to be exempt from paying can ask the lender, while borrowing, to pour him some water. Then the lender is working for him at that moment, which makes it שאילה בבעלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: someone who wants to borrow something from his friend and be exempt should say to him, 'Pour me some water.' Then it is borrowing together with the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives practical advice. A borrower can set things up so that he will not have to pay if the item gets damaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a borrower who also borrows or hires the owner's service at the same time is exempt. By asking the lender to do a small job right then, the borrower creates that situation. Even a tiny favor like pouring water is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrowing while the owner is also working for the borrower; the borrower is exempt
Pour me water / give me water to drink

phrases.english: Rava says:
One who wants to borrow
something from his friend and be exempt,
let him say to him: Pour me water,
since it is then borrowing with the owner.
phrases.notes: This is the rule from שמות 22:14: if the owner is with him, the borrower does not pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמִישְׁאַל מִידֵּי מֵחַבְרֵיהּ וְלִיפְּטַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: using the rule of שאילה בבעלים in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking the lender to do even a small service at the time of borrowing makes it שאילה בבעלים, so the borrower is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: The owner's work must be happening at the moment of borrowing. That timing is exactly what the next step uses.

steps.title: The clever lender's answer: 'Borrow first'
steps.stepSummary: A smart lender can block the trick. He tells the borrower to borrow first, and only afterward he will pour the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the lender is clever, he should say to him: 'Borrow first, and then I will pour for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues and shows how the lender can protect himself from the borrower's trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאילה בבעלים works only if the owner's service starts at the time of borrowing. If the lender pours the water only after the borrowing has already happened, the exemption does not apply, and the borrower stays liable.

phrases.english: And if he is clever,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the lender, who doesn't want the borrower to get off free.

phrases.english: let him say to him: Borrow first
and then I will pour for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי פִּקֵּחַ הוּא, נֵימָא לֵיהּ: שְׁאֵיל בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the lender a counter-move to the borrower's trick in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner's service begins only after the borrowing, it is not שאילה בבעלים, and the borrower is liable.

steps.title: Town workers count as 'working for you' during work hours
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists town workers: a children's teacher, gardener, butcher, bloodletter, and town scribe. Borrowing from any of them during their work hours counts as שאילה בבעלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a teacher of children, a gardener, a butcher, a bloodletter, and a town scribe: all of them, during their work time, are treated like borrowing with the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a list of people who are always counted as working for the people of their town while they are on the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These workers serve the whole town, so during work hours they are treated as being in the townspeople's service. If a townsperson borrows something from one of them then, it counts as שאילה בבעלים, and he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of their work

phrases.english: Rava says:
A teacher of children, a gardener,
a butcher, and a bloodletter, a town scribe –
all of them, at the time of their work,
are like borrowing with the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַקְרֵי דַרְדְּקֵי, שַׁתָּלָא, טַבָּחָא, וְאוּמָּנָא, סַפַּר מָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the topic of שאילה בבעלים to town workers, who are always counted as working for the townspeople during work hours.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing from these town workers during their work hours counts as שאילה בבעלים, so the borrower is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: שאילה בבעלים depends on the owner being in the borrower's service at the time of borrowing. A favor at that moment counts, a favor afterward does not, and town workers count automatically during work hours.
steps.whyThisMatters: These cases show that the exemption depends on timing and on real service, not just on the owner being physically present.

steps.title: The Rabbis claim רבא is lent to them
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבא that a teacher is 'lent' to his students. They use the same idea as the town workers in רבא's own list.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to רבא: Master, you are lent to us.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן apply רבא's own rule to רבא himself. They argue that since he works for them by teaching, borrowing from him should count as שאילה בבעלים. This sets up רבא's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, רבא said town workers are 'lent' to the town during their work hours. The students say a רב who teaches them is the same. If that were true, they would be exempt if something they borrowed from him broke or died.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, here meaning רבא's students and colleagues
Lent to us, working for us
Master, a respectful way to address a teacher

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
Master, you are lent to us.
phrases.notes: They mean: you work for us by teaching, just like the town workers רבא just listed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: שְׁאִיל לַן מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the town-worker rule from step 10 to a Torah teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students claim that a teacher is lent to his students.

steps.title: רבא says the students are lent to him
steps.stepSummary: רבא gets upset and turns the claim around: the students are lent to him, because he chooses what to teach and they cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got upset. He said to them: You want to take away my money?! On the contrary, you are lent to me. For I can switch you from one tractate to another, but you cannot switch me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the students' claim. He argues that they serve him, not the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is who controls the work. רבא can move from one מסכתא to another as he likes, and the students must follow. So he is not working for them, and borrowing from him is not שאילה בבעלים.

keyTerms.meaning: To slip away, to switch topics

phrases.english: He got upset.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לְאַפְקוֹעֵי מָמוֹנַאי קָא בָעֵיתוּ?!
phrases.english: He said to them: You want to take away my money?!
On the contrary, you are lent to me.
For whereas I can slip away from you
from tractate to tractate,
you cannot slip away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִקְּפִיד. אֲמַר לְהוּ: לְאַפְקוֹעֵי מָמוֹנַאי קָא בָעֵיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the students' claim from step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a teacher is lent to his students.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The one who controls the subject is the one being served, and the teacher controls the subject.

steps.title: During the כלה the teacher is lent to the students
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבא's answer is not fully right. During the כלה days the teacher is lent to the students, and during the rest of the year they are lent to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not so. He is lent to them during the days of the kallah. They are lent to him during the rest of the days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא and limits his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the כלה, the public study gatherings, the subject is fixed and the teacher must teach it. He can no longer switch topics, so by רבא's own test he is lent to them. Only the rest of the year are the students lent to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of the כלה, public Torah gatherings

steps.whatToRemember: The question of who is 'lent' to whom depends on who controls the work. During the כלה the teacher is lent to the students; the rest of the year they are lent to him.

phrases.english: But it is not so.
He is lent to them on the days of the kallah.
phrases.notes: At those gatherings the topic is set ahead of time, so the teacher can't switch.

phrases.english: They are lent to him on the rest of the days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's answer from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's claim as a rule for every day of the year.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: During the כלה the teacher cannot switch topics, so his own test makes him lent to the students.

steps.title: A rented mule dies and רבא rules the renters liable
steps.stepSummary: מרימר בר חנינא rented out a mule and went out with the renters when its load was put on. They were negligent, the mule died, and רבא ruled them liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר בר חנינא rented out a mule in בי חוזאי. He went out with them to lift its load. They were negligent with it and it died. They came before רבא, and he held them liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about whether the owner was 'with' his animal. This sets up the רבנן's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner seemed to be working with the renters when the load was put on, which looks like בבעלים. Even so, רבא held the renters liable for their negligence.

keyTerms.meaning: To lift its load onto it

phrases.aramaic: מָרִימָר בַּר חֲנִינָא אוֹגַר כּוּדַנְיָיתָא בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: Mareimar bar Chanina rented out a mule to people of Bei Chozai,
he went out to lift its load with them,
they were negligent with it and it died.
They came before Rava; he held them liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר בַּר חֲנִינָא אוֹגַר כּוּדַנְיָיתָא בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, also about whether the owner was 'with' his property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא held the renters liable for the mule that died through their negligence.

steps.title: The Rabbis object that the owner was with the mule
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבא that this is פשיעה בבעלים, so the renters should be exempt. רבא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to רבא: It is negligence while the owner was with it! He was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבא's ruling, and he seems to accept that he made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the owner was helping with the load, the רבנן see this as בבעלים. In their view, even negligence is exempt in that case. רבא's embarrassment shows he thought he had ruled wrongly.

keyTerms.meaning: Negligence while the owner was working with the one who has the item

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
It is negligence with the owner present!
He was embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: פְּשִׁיעָה בִּבְעָלִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the renters are liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner was working with them, so it is בבעלים, and negligence in that case is exempt.

steps.title: The owner was only supervising
steps.stepSummary: Later it came out that מרימר had only gone out to check the load, not to work. So it was not בבעלים, and רבא's ruling was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end it was revealed that he had gone out only to supervise the load.
steps.whatsHappening: New facts come out, and they support רבא's original ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only watching is not the same as working for the renter. Without real work by the owner there is no בבעלים, so the renters stay liable for their negligence.
steps.confusionAlert: The owner being physically there is not enough. He has to be actually working for the renter for it to count as בבעלים.

phrases.english: In the end the matter was revealed
that he had gone out to supervise its load.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אִיגַּלַּאי מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 15 with new facts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner was working with them, so it was בבעלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only supervising, so it was not בבעלים, and the renters are liable.

steps.title: Why was רבא embarrassed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא was embarrassed according to the opinion that פשיעה בבעלים is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says negligence with the owner present is exempt; that is why he was embarrassed. But for the one who says it is liable, why was he embarrassed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the story to raise a question about a known disagreement. It sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about whether פשיעה בבעלים is exempt or liable. If it is exempt, it makes sense that רבא was embarrassed. If it is liable, his ruling was correct even in a בבעלים case, so he had nothing to be embarrassed about.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
negligence with the owner present is exempt;
that is why he was embarrassed.
But according to the one who says liable,
why was he embarrassed?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פְּשִׁיעָה בִּבְעָלִים פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of רבא's embarrassment in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's embarrassment, according to the opinion that פשיעה בבעלים is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If negligence is liable even בבעלים, רבא's ruling was right either way, so he had no reason to be embarrassed.

steps.title: The story is retold: the mule was stolen, not neglected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from Step 17 by changing the details of the story. The renters were not negligent. The mule was stolen and died naturally in the thief's house, and רבא held the renters liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were not negligent with it. Rather, it was stolen, and it died naturally in the thief's house. They came before רבא and he held them liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why רבא was embarrassed by saying the story really happened differently: the case was about theft, not negligence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that פשיעה בבעלים is still liable, so under that view the case as first told gave רבא nothing to be embarrassed about. The new version turns the case into theft. That sets up the רבנן's objection in the next step, which works according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It died naturally, not because of anything someone did

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new story. It is the same story about מרימר's mule, with the details corrected to explain why רבא was embarrassed.

phrases.english: They were not negligent with it,
phrases.notes: "They" are the renters of מרימר's mule from Step 14.

phrases.english: rather, it was stolen,
and it died naturally; it was in the thief's house.
And they came before רבא
and he held them liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיפְשָׁע פְּשַׁעוּ בָּהּ, אֶלָּא אִיגְּנוֹבֵי אִיגְּנוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's question by changing the facts of the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was about negligence, so under the view that פשיעה בבעלים is liable, רבא had no reason to be embarrassed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case was really about theft, which allows an objection that works according to everyone.

steps.title: The Rabbis object that this is theft with the owner present
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבא that this is גניבה בבעלים, theft while the owner was working with the renters, so the renters should be exempt. רבא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to רבא: It is theft with the owner. He was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבא's ruling. Because the owner had gone out with the renters, they say the case is exempt, and רבא is embarrassed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about negligence with the owner present, but for theft with the owner present, everyone agrees the renter is exempt. So now the objection works according to everyone, and that explains why רבא was embarrassed.

keyTerms.meaning: Theft that happens while the owner is working together with the borrower or renter, which makes him exempt

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to רבא:
It is theft with the owner.
phrases.notes: They mean the owner went out with the renters, so they should be exempt.

phrases.english: He was embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling described in the corrected story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the renters are liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner went out with the renters, so this is גניבה בבעלים, which is exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: The owner had only gone out to check the load
steps.stepSummary: In the end it became clear that מרימר had gone out only to check the load, not to work with the renters. So it was not בבעלים, and רבא's ruling was correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end the matter was revealed: he had gone out to check its load.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by showing that רבא was right after all, because the owner was not really working for the renters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption of בבעלים applies only when the owner is working for the borrower or renter. Checking the load is not that kind of work, so the renters were liable for the theft, as רבא ruled.
steps.whatToRemember: The exemption of בבעלים applies only when the owner is actually working for the borrower or renter. If he is just present to check things, the exemption does not apply.

phrases.english: In the end the matter was revealed
that it was to check its load that he went out.
phrases.notes: "He" is מרימר, the owner. He only inspected the load and did not work for the renters.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אִיגַּלַּאי מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's objection and shows רבא's ruling was right.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner was working with the renters, so the theft was בבעלים and exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner only checked the load, so it was not בבעלים, and the renters are liable.

steps.title: New משנה: a cow that was partly borrowed and partly rented dies
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes cases where the same person both borrowed and rented a cow, at different times or as two different cows, and a cow died. The lender begins to claim that it died while it was borrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who borrows a cow: he borrowed it for half a day and rented it for half a day, or borrowed it today and rented it tomorrow, or rented one and borrowed one, and it died. The lender says: The borrowed one died, it died on the day it was borrowed...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with cases where a cow died and it is not clear whether it was borrowed or rented at the time. This step sets up the claims, and the sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower (שואל) pays even if the animal dies naturally, while a renter (שוכר) does not pay for a natural death. So it matters a lot whether the cow died during the borrowed time or the rented time, and the lender naturally claims it was the borrowed one.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה
The lender, the owner who lent it

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה gives three separate cases, not one long case: half-day and half-day, today and tomorrow, and two different cows.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who borrows a cow:
he borrowed it for half a day
and rented it for half a day.
Or he borrowed it today and rented it for tomorrow.
Or he rented one and borrowed one,
and it died.
phrases.notes: In each case, it is not clear whether the cow died while it was borrowed or while it was rented.

phrases.english: The lender says:
The borrowed one died,
or: it died on the day it was borrowed,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹאֵל אֶת הַפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up cases of doubt over whether a cow that died was borrowed or rented, and begins the lender's claim that it was borrowed.
